<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0904d856e31fd065c71af725cf3ad4ad0363dc76` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

This run read `content/docs` from `97c8167b6d834257636b543f33babd5890946add` — the merge of head `7fa022b591b0bdd4ac803ad0748d1e24eab071bc` into base `0904d856e31fd065c71af725cf3ad4ad0363dc76`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 97c8167b6d834257636b543f33babd5890946add && git checkout 97c8167b6d834257636b543f33babd5890946add
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0904d856e31fd065c71af725cf3ad4ad0363dc76 7fa022b591b0bdd4ac803ad0748d1e24eab071bc && git checkout -B drift-repro 0904d856e31fd065c71af725cf3ad4ad0363dc76 && git merge --no-ff 7fa022b591b0bdd4ac803ad0748d1e24eab071bc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0904d856e31fd065c71af725cf3ad4ad0363dc76
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0904d856e31fd065c71af725cf3ad4ad0363dc76` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · #24701 half (a) · `domain:services` seat 2 · `os-warren` · `session_01LR1cD9JqgkeqY7k9rrZH8s` · 2026-10-20T03:27Z · head `7fa022b591`, the review of record for claim `6281802681`.

1. **Form:**
   - Draft, base `main`. The first line is `Part of #24701`, and the body carries no closing keyword beside an issue number (seat grep: 0 hits).
   - `Clause-②: no` on the body and on the changeset's line.
   - One `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` and `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`.
   - 5 files, +158/−2. The card stays open for half (b).
2. **Premise, measured:**
   - **The diff.** The seat's own read: each `by_object` view loses its `grouping` key and nothing else. The `object_name, label` sort and the columns are unchanged, and each object gains a one-paragraph reason. `sys-record-share.object.ts`, `packages/spec` and the #15194 epic's files are untouched.
   - **The group header.** The seat read objectui at the console pin `12dc7b47c3`. `ObjectGrid`'s `groupValueFormatter` builds its labels from the field's `options` alone and has no widget arm. So a grouping on an `object-ref` field heads each group with the stored API name, as the card says.
   - **The pins.** Two new pins refuse a grouping on any field that stores an object API name: an `object-ref` widget, or a `referenceVia` type half. The sharing pin runs over every object in `objects/index.ts`, and each pin has a non-empty-set guard and a control case.
   - **Ablation.** One leg per file put the grouping back. Each went red in its own case (1 failed, 2 passed) and was restored to HEAD's blob with `git diff HEAD` empty.
3. **Gates:**
   - CI on `7fa022b591` at this read: 40 check-runs, 34 success, 6 skipped, 0 failed; mergeable `clean`. The six skips are path-filtered or opt-in: Dogfood Regression Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke. `check-expected-skips.mjs` could not run in the seat's container (its `yaml` import is not installed in the shared checkout, which the seat does not touch), so the seat judged these by name.
   - Local on the head: 67 derived, 66 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN (`--ran` exit 0).
     - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` needs a whole-workspace build. CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` runs it, and the diff touches no entry, export or build config.
     - `check:i18n` exited 0 on its rerun, after its own prescribed build.
   - Package suites:
     - `plugin-sharing`: 1172 tests.
     - `plugin-webhooks`: 215 tests.
     - Both typechecks exit 0, and the test-typecheck ledgers are unchanged.
   - The seat's diff read: both test files are new, so no existing `expect(` line is removed.
4. **Accepted deviations:**
   - `origin/main` moved 6 commits during the run. None touches either plugin or `packages/spec`, so the branch was not merged.
   - The sharing pin's set case lists the API-name fields of every shipped sharing object. A new object in `objects/index.ts` turns it red until its fields are listed. That is the point of the enumeration, and the overlap with #24611's grouping case in `sharing-pointer-pairs.test.ts` is deliberate.
   - The commit carries the repository's model-free attribution pair, per AGENTS.md.
5. **Out of scope:**
   - **Half (b)** (the record share's heading and Recipient column): ruled by the seat in `6282390889` (route B, a display declaration). It is this card's next dispatch, after this PR lands.
   - **Acceptance notes item 1** (the console's group header does not use cell faces): Acceptance notes. After this PR, no served objectstack view groups on such a field, and the pins hold that. `carrier: none`.
   - **Acceptance notes item 2** (the Recipient column's raw id): carried by half (b) above.
6. **Landing:** ordinary queue landing (`check-governed-merges`: not governed, 160 lines). When every check on the current head is green, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay, then confirms MERGED. The card keeps `pm:dispatched` for half (b).
